## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the calibration, operation, and maintenance of
handheld nephelometric turbidity meters for field measurement of water
clarity. Turbidity is a measure of the optical scattering caused by
suspended particles (sediment, algae, organic matter) and is a
standard water quality parameter required by the Surface Water Ambient
Monitoring Program (SWAMP), NPDES permits, and many ecological
studies. Field turbidity measurements complement laboratory analysis
by providing an immediate, on-site result.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Handheld nephelometric turbidity meters (e.g., Hach
  2100Q, LaMotte 2020we, Oakton T-100) used for in situ and grab-
  sample turbidity measurements at EA Program field sites
- **Does not apply to:** Laboratory bench-top turbidimeters; Secchi
  disk transparency measurements (see
  [SOP-F207](SOP-F207-secchi-disk.qmd)); continuous turbidity
  sensors deployed on multiparameter sondes (see
  [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd))
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water field sites


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve instrument selection; review QC data            |
| Trained Personnel | Calibrate and operate the meter per this SOP            |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Sampling near water involves slip and fall hazards.
- **Biological:** Water samples may contain pathogens. Wear gloves.
- **Chemical:** Calibration standards (formazin or StablCal) are mild
  irritants. Do not ingest. Formazin contains hydrazine; handle with
  gloves and dispose of as hazardous waste.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (during calibration)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). For
formazin contact with skin or eyes, flush with water for at least 15
minutes and consult the SDS.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Handheld turbidity meter              | Confirm model and battery level          |
| Calibration standards                 | Hach StablCal (sealed vials): < 0.1, 20, 100, 800 NTU; or formazin dilution series |
| Sample vials (matched to instrument)  | Glass or optical-grade; use only with the meter they were supplied for |
| Silicone oil and applicator cloth     | For coating sample vials to reduce light scattering from scratches |
| Lint-free wipes (Kimwipes)            | For cleaning vials                       |
| DI water (squeeze bottle)             | For rinsing vials                        |
| Waste container (for formazin)        | Labeled for hazardous waste              |
| Field notebook                        | For recording calibration and measurements |
| Spare batteries                       | Matched to meter model                   |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Calibration

Calibrate the meter at the start of each field day or when the
instrument has been stored for more than one week.

1. Turn on the meter and allow it to warm up (approximately 1 minute).
2. Clean the outside of each calibration standard vial with a lint-free
   wipe. Apply a thin film of silicone oil and wipe evenly.
3. Insert the lowest standard (< 0.1 NTU) into the sample chamber
   with the orientation mark aligned. Close the lid.
4. Press **Cal** (or follow the on-screen prompts for the specific
   model). The meter reads the standard and stores the value.
5. Repeat with each subsequent standard in ascending order (e.g.,
   20, 100, 800 NTU).
6. When all standards have been read, the meter confirms a successful
   calibration. Record the calibration date, standard lot number,
   and any correction factors in the field notebook.
7. Verify the calibration by re-reading the 20 NTU standard. The
   reading should be within +/- 10% of 20 NTU. If not, repeat the
   calibration.

### 6.2 Sample Collection

1. Collect a grab sample in a clean container (glass jar or
   polypropylene bottle). Follow the procedures in
   [SOP-F300 Surface Water Sampling](SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd).
2. Avoid disturbing bottom sediments during collection.
3. Analyze the sample as soon as possible. If a delay is unavoidable,
   keep the sample in the dark to prevent algal growth and analyze
   within 24 hours.

### 6.3 Measurement

1. Gently invert the sample container 3--4 times to resuspend
   particles uniformly. Do not shake vigorously (creates bubbles).
2. Pour the sample into a clean sample vial, filling to the line.
3. Cap the vial and let it sit for 1 minute to allow large air
   bubbles to rise.
4. Wipe the outside of the vial with a lint-free cloth. Apply
   silicone oil if using glass vials.
5. Insert the vial into the sample chamber with the orientation mark
   aligned. Close the lid completely.
6. Press **Read**. Wait for the display to stabilize.
7. Record the result (NTU) in the field notebook along with the
   sample ID, time, and site.
8. For samples above the meter range (typically > 1000 NTU), dilute
   with DI water, measure, and multiply by the dilution factor.
   Record both the diluted reading and the calculated result.
9. Rinse the vial 3 times with DI water between samples.

### 6.4 Post-Field Care

1. Rinse all sample vials with DI water and allow to air-dry inverted.
2. Wipe silicone oil residue from vials before storage.
3. Store calibration standards in their original case at room
   temperature, away from direct sunlight.
4. Turn off the meter and remove batteries if storing for more than
   one month.


## 7. Quality Control

- Calibrate at the start of each field day (Section 6.1).
- Measure a DI water blank at the start and end of each sampling event.
  The blank should read < 1 NTU.
- Measure one field duplicate per 10 samples (minimum one per event).
  Duplicate RPD should be < 20% for readings above 10 NTU.
- If the meter reading drifts (DI blank reads > 1 NTU during the
  day), recalibrate and re-measure the most recent samples.
- Inspect sample vials for scratches before each use. Replace scratched
  vials, as scratches scatter light and produce false high readings.


## 8. References

- Hach Company. *2100Q Portable Turbidimeter User Manual*.

## 10. Training Record

Before using turbidity meters independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate a complete calibration using StablCal or formazin
   standards
3. Perform supervised field measurements at one site
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
